ukmt-maclaurin-2022-m1.title: Pulp stays constant
ukmt-maclaurin-2022-m1.body:
Take $100$ units of fruit: $m$ of water and $100-m$ of pulp. After drying, the water is $m\left(1-\frac{m-5}{100}\right)=\frac{m(105-m)}{100}$ and the pulp is unchanged. A $50\%$ water content means water equals pulp:
$$\frac{m(105-m)}{100}=100-m\ \Longrightarrow\ m^2-205m+10000=0\ \Longrightarrow\ (m-80)(m-125)=0 .$$
Since $m\le100$, $m=80$.

Check: $80$ water, $20$ pulp; it loses $75\%$ of the water, leaving $20$ water and $20$ pulp: $50\%$ ✓.

**Answer: $80$**

ukmt-maclaurin-2022-m2.title: Factorise $k^3+1$
ukmt-maclaurin-2022-m2.body:
**(i)** $(x+1)(x^2-x+1)=x^3-x^2+x+x^2-x+1=x^3+1$.

**(ii)** Suppose $2^n=k^3+1$ for an integer $k$. Since $2^n\ge1$, $k\ge0$. By (i),
$$2^n=(k+1)(k^2-k+1).$$
Both factors are positive integers dividing $2^n$, so both are powers of $2$. But $k^2-k+1=k(k-1)+1$ is always odd ($k(k-1)$ is even), so $k^2-k+1=1$, i.e. $k(k-1)=0$, so $k=0$ or $k=1$. Then $2^n=1$ or $2^n=2$.

Check: $1=0^3+1$ and $2=1^3+1$.

**Answer: (i) $x^3+1$; (ii) the powers $1$ and $2$.** ∎

ukmt-maclaurin-2022-m3.title: Arithmetic progressions of sides
ukmt-maclaurin-2022-m3.body:
If one side is the mean of the other two, then the sides form an arithmetic progression: $y-d,\ y,\ y+d$ with $d\ge0$ an integer and $y>0$. The triangle inequality $(y-d)+y>y+d$ becomes $y>2d$.

One of the sides equals $10$:

- **$y=10$:** $10>2d$, so $d=0,1,2,3,4$: $(10,10,10),(9,10,11),(8,10,12),(7,10,13),(6,10,14)$ — $5$ triangles.
- **$y-d=10$, $d\ge1$:** $y=10+d>2d$, so $d=1,\dots,9$: sides $(10,10+d,10+2d)$ — $9$ triangles.
- **$y+d=10$, $d\ge1$:** $y=10-d>2d$, so $d<\tfrac{10}3$, $d=1,2,3$: $(8,9,10),(6,8,10),(4,7,10)$ — $3$ triangles.

The three families are disjoint (the middle length is $10$, the smallest is $10$ with middle $>10$, the largest is $10$), so the total is $5+9+3=17$.

**Answer: $17$**

ukmt-maclaurin-2022-m4.title: Four patterns repeated in every triple
ukmt-maclaurin-2022-m4.body:
Let the number of moves be $3k$ ($k\ge1$). Split the moves into $k$ triples; the $j$th triple ($j=0,\dots,k-1$) consists of moves of lengths $8^j\cdot1,\ 8^j\cdot2,\ 8^j\cdot4$. Put $S=1+8+\dots+8^{k-1}$.

Choose a pattern for the directions within a triple and use the **same** pattern in every triple:

- $EEE$: the robot goes $7S$ East in total: distance $7S$.
- $NNN$: $7S$ North: distance $7S$.
- $EEN$: East $(1+2)S=3S$, North $4S$; distance $\sqrt{(3S)^2+(4S)^2}=5S$.
- $NNE$: North $3S$, East $4S$; distance $5S$.

These four routes are different (their first moves and patterns differ), and each ends at an integer distance from the origin. ∎

ukmt-maclaurin-2022-m5.title: Use the discriminants
ukmt-maclaurin-2022-m5.body:
**(i)** If $x^2+bx+c$ has integer roots $u\ne v$, then $b^2-4c=(u-v)^2=p^2$ with $p=|u-v|$ a positive integer. Similarly $x^2+bx-c$ has integer roots $u'\ne v'$, so $b^2+4c=q^2$ with $q=|u'-v'|$ a positive integer. Adding: $2b^2=p^2+q^2$. Also $q^2-p^2=8c\ne0$ so $p\ne q$.

**(ii)** Assume $p>q$. As $p^2+q^2=2b^2$ is even, $p$ and $q$ have the same parity, so $r=\dfrac{p+q}2$ and $s=\dfrac{p-q}2$ are integers, with $r>s>0$ (since $q>0$). Then $p=r+s$, $q=r-s$ and
$$2b^2=p^2+q^2=(r+s)^2+(r-s)^2=2r^2+2s^2,$$
so $b^2=r^2+s^2$. ∎

ukmt-maclaurin-2022-m6.title: Similar triangles
ukmt-maclaurin-2022-m6.body:
The angles $\angle BAC$ and $\angle BDC$ stand on the same arc $BC$ (with $A,D$ on the same side of $BC$), so $\angle BDC=\angle BAC=\angle CED$.

Triangles $CED$ and $CDB$ share the angle at $C$ ($\angle ECD=\angle BCD$, as $E$ lies on $BC$) and have $\angle CED=\angle CDB$. So $\triangle CED\sim\triangle CDB$ (with $E\leftrightarrow D$, $D\leftrightarrow B$), hence
$$\frac{CE}{CD}=\frac{CD}{CB}=\frac{ED}{DB}.$$
From $CD^2=CE\cdot CB=CE\cdot4CE=4CE^2$ we get $CD=2CE$. Therefore $\dfrac{ED}{DB}=\dfrac{CE}{CD}=\dfrac12$, i.e. $DB=2\,DE$. ∎
